  • Rom. 3:27. "Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith" — no flesh glories in His presence; the ground of acceptance is faith, not performance.
  • Rom. 3:28. "Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law" — the apostolic conclusion stated as doctrine: justification is by faith, wholly apart from the deeds of the law.
  • Rom. 5:1. "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ" — the immediate fruit: a settled standing, peace that rests on Another's righteousness and therefore cannot be shaken by our own record.
  • FLB 107.2. White: "The grace of Christ is freely to justify the sinner without merit or claim on his part. Justification is a full, complete pardon of sin. The moment a sinner accepts Christ by faith, that moment he is pardoned. The righteousness of Christ is imputed to him, and he is no more to doubt God's forgiving grace." — justification defined: full pardon, imputed righteousness, received the moment faith accepts, "without merit or claim" on the sinner's part.
  • FW 103.2. White: "Pardon and justification are one and the same thing. Through faith, the believer passes from the position of a rebel, a child of sin and Satan, to the position of a loyal subject of Christ Jesus, not because of an inherent goodness, but because Christ receives him as His child by adoption." — the rebel changes standing on Christ's account, not his own; no inherent goodness enters the transaction.

Counted for righteousness — the imputed title — Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4:3-5, 22-25:

  • Gen. 15:6. "And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness." — the gospel's original arithmetic, laid down in Moses: faith COUNTED for righteousness; justification by faith is no New Testament innovation but the covenant from the beginning.
    • imputed for righteousness / counted / reckoned = to credit to the believer's account a righteousness he did not earn — the legal ground of the believer's title to heaven (Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4:3-5; Rom. 4:22-25; 2 Cor. 5:21; Phil. 3:9).
  • Rom. 4:3. "For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness." — Paul rests his whole case on "what saith the scripture"; the doctrine is as old as Abraham.
  • Rom. 4:4. "Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt." — earnings are wages, and wages are debt; God is made debtor to no man — so a righteousness earned would be no gift at all.
  • Rom. 4:5. "But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness." — the scandal and the glory of the gospel: God justifies the UNGODLY who believe; the working stops, and the counting begins.
  • Rom. 4:22-23. "And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness. Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him" — Abraham's ledger is a specimen page written for the world, not a private privilege.
  • Rom. 4:24. "But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead" — the same crediting, on the same terms, to every believer now.
  • Rom. 4:25. "Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification." — the ground of the imputed title is not a fiction but the delivered-up and risen Christ Himself.
  • FW 18.1. White: "The point that has been urged upon my mind for years is the imputed righteousness of Christ... I have made it the subject of nearly every discourse and talk that I have given to the people." — imputed righteousness is the Heaven-urged burden of the message, not a peripheral point.
  • CIHS 48.2. White: "The incense, ascending with the prayers of Israel, represents the merits and intercession of Christ, His perfect righteousness, which through faith is imputed to His people, and which can alone make the worship of sinful beings acceptable to God." — the sanctuary preaches the same doctrine: imputed righteousness ALONE makes a sinner's worship acceptable.

The righteousness is a Person — Jer. 23:6; 1 Cor. 1:30; Phil. 3:9; 2 Cor. 5:21:

  • Jer. 23:6. "In his days Judah shall be saved... and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS." — the Messiah's own name settles the question forever: our righteousness is not a quality we manufacture but a Person we receive.
  • 1 Cor. 1:30. "But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption" — the same Christ is MADE UNTO US both righteousness (the imputed title) and sanctification (the imparted fitness): one Person supplies both, and there is no righteousness of any kind apart from being "in Christ Jesus."
  • Phil. 3:9. "And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith" — Paul the Pharisee throws his own law-righteousness away to be "found in him," wearing a righteousness whose whole origin is God.
  • 2 Cor. 5:21. "For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him." — the great exchange, imputation in its sharpest form: our sin laid on the Sinless One, that His righteousness be MADE ours "in him."
  • DA 300.1. White: "The proud heart strives to earn salvation; but both our title to heaven and our fitness for it are found in the righteousness of Christ." — the exact frame of this section: TITLE (imputed) and FITNESS (imparted), both found in His righteousness, neither self-earned.
  • CHR 62.1. Waggoner: "At last the sinner, weary of the vain struggle to get righteousness from the law, listens to the voice of Christ and flees to His outstretched arms. Hiding in Christ, he is covered with His righteousness... With the righteousness which is 'through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith' (Philippians 3:9), Paul was sure that he would stand secure in the day of Christ." — the 1888 messenger on Phil. 3:9: the vain striving ends where the covering begins, and the covered man possesses the very righteousness the law requires.

The just shall live by faith — Hab. 2:4; Rom. 1:16-17:

  • Hab. 2:4. "Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith." — the two ways set side by side: the self-lifted soul is not upright in him; the just man LIVES — from justification onward — by his faith.
    • the just shall live by faith = the believer enters righteousness by faith and continues the entire Christian life by that same faith — total dependence on the word of God; the just man lives by precisely the principle by which he became just (Hab. 2:4; Rom. 1:17; Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4:3-5).
  • Rom. 1:16. "For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth" — the gospel is not advice but POWER, God's own power, unto salvation — the deliverance from sin walked in "What Salvation Really Is — Saved From Sin."
  • Rom. 1:17. "For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith." — the righteousness revealed is GOD'S, not man's, and it is received "from faith to faith" — faith at the gate and faith the whole way; the banner text of the Reformation and of 1888.
  • LOF_ATJ 38.8. Jones: "Men must not only become just by faith—by dependence upon the word of God—but being just, we must live by faith. The just man lives in precisely the same way and by precisely the same thing that he becomes just." — righteousness by faith is continuous, not a one-time transaction followed by law-works.
  • LOF_ATJ 38.9. Jones: "We become just by faith; faith is entire dependence on the word of God. We, being just, must live by precisely the same thing by which we become just; that is, by entire dependence upon the word of God." — the faith that justifies and the faith that sanctifies are one faith, and Jones defines it: entire dependence on the word of God.

Imparted — Christ living in the believer — Gal. 2:20; Rom. 8:3-4; Gal. 5:6:

  • Gal. 2:20. "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me." — the formula of imparted righteousness: the old "I" crucified, and the life now lived is Christ's own life within — the surrendered life entered at the new birth (see "Born of Water and of the Spirit — How He Lived, How We Begin").
  • Rom. 8:3. "For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh" — what the law could not do in flesh it was weak through, God did IN that very flesh: the Son came into the nature where sin had reigned and condemned sin there (see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took").
  • Rom. 8:4. "That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit." — the stated purpose of the whole remedy: the law's righteousness fulfilled IN us — imputed righteousness never stops short of imparted obedience; real obedience is the design, never an option.
  • Gal. 5:6. "For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love." — the faith that justifies is never a dead assent: it WORKS, and works by love — the imparted life is the living activity of the very faith that received the title.

Works — excluded as the root, required as the fruit — Eph. 2:8-10; James 2:17-18:

  • Eph. 2:8. "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God" — salvation whole is the gift of God: grace the source, faith the receiving hand, and even that not of ourselves.
  • Eph. 2:9. "Not of works, lest any man should boast." — works shut out at the root, absolutely; boasting is left no ground to stand on.
  • Eph. 2:10. "For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them." — the same breath that shuts works out as the root ordains them as the fruit: the saved man is God's WORKMANSHIP, created unto good works — this is the balance the whole section owns.
  • James 2:17. "Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone." — the guard against the counterfeit: a workless "faith" is a corpse, and a corpse justifies no one.
  • James 2:18. "shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works" — works are faith's only visible evidence — the proof of the living faith, never its purchase price.
  • AA 563.1. White: "John did not teach that salvation was to be earned by obedience; but that obedience was the fruit of faith and love... The sanctified heart is in harmony with the precepts of God's law." — the balance in one line: obedience the fruit, never the root — and the sanctified heart really does harmonize with the law.
  • COL 312.2. White: "Righteousness is right doing, and it is by their deeds that all will be judged. Our characters are revealed by what we do. The works show whether the faith is genuine." — the judgment reads the works because the works read the faith.

The message identified — Minneapolis, 1888, and the verity — 1SM 372:

  • 1SM 372.2. White: "Several have written to me, inquiring if the message of justification by faith is the third angel's message, and I have answered, 'It is the third angel's message, in verity.'" — the definitive identification (The Review and Herald, April 1, 1890): the message of justification by faith proclaimed by E. J. Waggoner and A. T. Jones at the 1888 Minneapolis General Conference is not a theme beside the third angel's message but that message itself, in verity — the gospel content of the third angel, whose fruit is walked in "The Commandments of God and the Faith of Jesus."
  • 1SM 372.1. White: "there is no danger in presenting this doctrine as it is set forth in the Scriptures. If there had not been a remissness in the past to properly instruct the people of God, there would not now be a necessity of calling a special attention to it." — righteousness by faith is to be preached fully and fearlessly, "as it is set forth in the Scriptures"; the "special attention" was owed to past neglect, not to novelty.

DEFINITION — RIGHTEOUSNESS BY FAITH — THE THIRD ANGEL’S MESSAGE IN VERITY = Christ's own righteousness given to the believer in two inseparable modes. IMPUTED: his faith is "counted... for righteousness" (Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4:3-5), written "for us also, to whom it shall be imputed" (Rom. 4:22-25) — the believer is "justified freely by his grace" through faith in Christ's blood, "without the deeds of the law," so that God is at once "just, and the justifier" (Rom. 3:24-28); the sinless One was "made... sin for us... that we might be made the righteousness of God in him" (2 Cor. 5:21); this is the believer's TITLE, and its fruit is peace with God (Rom. 5:1; FLB 107.2; FW 103.2). IMPARTED: the same Christ made unto us "righteousness, and sanctification" (1 Cor. 1:30) lives His own life in the believer — "not I, but Christ liveth in me" (Gal. 2:20) — fulfilling the righteousness of the law IN us in the very flesh where He condemned sin (Rom. 8:3-4; see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took"), through "faith which worketh by love" (Gal. 5:6); this is the believer's FITNESS, and "both our title to heaven and our fitness for it are found in the righteousness of Christ" (DA 300.1). It is "the righteousness of God," not man's (Rom. 1:17; 3:21-22; Phil. 3:9); its very Name is THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS (Jer. 23:6); it is entered by faith and lived by that same faith — entire dependence on the word of God (Hab. 2:4; LOF_ATJ 38.8-9) — and its works are excluded as the root of salvation and required as its fruit (Eph. 2:8-10; James 2:17-18; AA 563.1; COL 312.2). This message, carried by Waggoner and Jones from Minneapolis in 1888, is "the third angel's message, in verity" (1SM 372.2): the remedy that saves FROM sin (see "What Salvation Really Is — Saved From Sin"), provides the complete victory walked in "Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame," and ripens the commandment-keeping people of "The Commandments of God and the Faith of Jesus."

Symbols defined here:

  • righteousness by faith = Christ's own righteousness given to the believer in two inseparable modes: IMPUTED — His obedience counted to the believer, the title (Gen. 15:6; Rom. 3:24-28; Rom. 4:3-5, 22-25; 2 Cor. 5:21; Phil. 3:9); and IMPARTED — Christ living in the believer by faith, fulfilling the law's righteousness in him, the fitness (Rom. 8:3-4; Gal. 2:20; Gal. 5:6; 1 Cor. 1:30; DA 300.1). Its Name is THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS (Jer. 23:6); obedience is its fruit, never its root, and never optional (Eph. 2:8-10; James 2:17-18).
  • imputed for righteousness / counted / reckoned = to credit to the believer's account a righteousness he did not earn — faith "counted... for righteousness" to him "that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly"; the legal ground of the believer's title (Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4:3-5; Rom. 4:22-25; 2 Cor. 5:21; FW 18.1).
  • the just shall live by faith = the believer becomes just by faith and continues the whole Christian life by that same faith — entire dependence on the word of God; self-lifted works excluded from first to last (Hab. 2:4; Rom. 1:16-17; LOF_ATJ 38.8-9).

Symbols carried: sin = consented transgression of the law — the thing pardoned in justification and dethroned by the indwelling Christ (see "What Sin Is — Transgression, Not Inheritance"); sinful flesh and the second Adam — the very nature in which the Son came and "condemned sin in the flesh" (Rom. 8:3; see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took"); the new birth — the entrance into the "not I, but Christ" life (Gal. 2:20; see "Born of Water and of the Spirit — How He Lived, How We Begin"); salvation = God saving His people FROM their sins, the deliverance this righteousness works (see "What Salvation Really Is — Saved From Sin"). The victory this faith provides is walked in "Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame," and the people it ripens in "The Commandments of God and the Faith of Jesus."

For discussion:

  1. "Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness" (Rom. 4:4-5). Where in your religious life are you quietly working for wages — treating obedience, devotions, or reform as a claim on God — and what would change today if both your title and your fitness were sought only in the righteousness of Christ (DA 300.1)?
  2. Jones says the just man "lives in precisely the same way and by precisely the same thing that he becomes just" (LOF_ATJ 38.8; Hab. 2:4; Rom. 1:17, "from faith to faith"). Many begin by faith and then continue by effort. How do you tell the difference between obedience that is the fruit of living faith (Gal. 5:6; AA 563.1) and obedience that has quietly become the root — earning all over again?
  3. Ellen White answered that justification by faith "is the third angel's message, in verity" (1SM 372.2) and that "there is no danger in presenting this doctrine as it is set forth in the Scriptures" (1SM 372.1). Does the message you actually carry — in your home, your class, your witness — center where Heaven centered it: God "just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus" (Rom. 3:26)? If not, what neglected "special attention" does it need from you?

¶7. Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame

Must the believer always fall short, sinning and repenting till death? Scripture answers with a charter, not a wish: sin SHALL NOT have dominion; whatsoever is born of God overcometh; God is able to keep you from falling — the same victory Christ won, by the same faith, in the same flesh, "even as I also overcame."

The charter promise — sin dethroned — Rom. 6:6, 14, 22:

  • Rom. 6:14. "For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace." — the charter of this whole section: sin SHALL NOT rule the believer, stated as a future certainty, not a wish; grace, not law-under-condemnation, is the ground of the deliverance.
  • Rom. 6:6. "our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin" — the mechanism of the promise: union with the crucified Christ, not native effort; the body of sin destroyed so that we "should not serve sin" — "not I, but Christ liveth in me" (Gal. 2:20; see "Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel’s Message in Verity").
  • Rom. 6:22. "But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life" — the freedom is present and actual, bearing fruit unto holiness; the gospel result is genuine liberty from sin's service, not managed failure (see "What Salvation Really Is — Saved From Sin").
  • WOR 110.3. Waggoner, reading the whole of the fourteenth verse: "Sin has no dominion over those who yield themselves servants to righteousness... transgression of the law has no place in them who are not under the law" — sin's dominion is actually broken, not re-labeled.
  • WOR 198.5. Waggoner meets the objection of this section head-on: "A questioner may say, 'You make it out that we ought never to sin any more, - you leave no room for sin.' But is not that what the Bible says?... There is such a thing as a complete surrender to Christ, - when we give up everything, and then trust to his power to keep us in that state. And I thank God that he is able to do it." — the exact question of this section, answered from Rom. 6:14 itself: no, we ought never to sin any more, and Christ is able to keep the fully surrendered.

Born of God — the life that does not practise sin — 1 John 3:8-9; 5:4, 18:

  • 1 John 3:8. "For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil." — the incarnation's stated purpose is the undoing of sin in the believer, not its accommodation; a gospel that leaves sin reigning defeats the very errand of Bethlehem.
  • 1 John 3:9. "Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God." — while the divine seed remains, the born-of-God life does not practise sin — not a sinlessness native to the flesh apart from Christ, but the new-birth life that cannot sin so long as it abides in Him (see "Born of Water and of the Spirit — How He Lived, How We Begin").
  • 1 John 5:4. "For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith." — the overcomer defined, and the means named in the same breath: faith — the identical faith by which Christ Himself overcame.
    • the overcomer = one in whom the born-of-God life triumphs over sin and the world — not by native strength but by Christ living out in fallen flesh the very victory He Himself won (1 John 5:4, "even our faith"; 1 John 5:18, "keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not"; Rev. 3:21, "even as I also overcame"; Gal. 2:20, "not I, but Christ liveth in me"; Rom. 6:14, 22) — the normal Christian of Revelation's promises, "made free from sin," over whom sin "shall not have dominion."
  • 1 John 5:18. "whosoever is born of God sinneth not; but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and that wicked one toucheth him not" — kept, guarded, untouched; the overcomer's security is real, not aspirational.
  • CWCP 50.1. Jones: "That faith which He exercised and by which He obtained the victory over the world, the flesh, and the devil—that faith is His free gift to every lost man in the world. And thus 'this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.'" — the faith Christ exercised, by which He "trusted God for salvation from sin and power to keep from sinning," is His free gift to every lost man: the overcomer overcomes by Christ's own victory-faith, not by manufacture but by donation.

Provision complete — no temptation compels sin — Jude 24; 1 Cor. 10:13; 2 Cor. 2:14:

  • Jude 24. "Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy" — the keeping power and the faultless standing are both His work; falling is never made necessary.
  • 1 Cor. 10:13. "God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape" — with EVERY temptation a guaranteed exit: no temptation ever compels sin; sin is therefore always avoidable, and every fall is a way of escape not taken.
  • 2 Cor. 2:14. "Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ" — ALWAYS, with no exception clause for necessary defeat; triumph, not managed failure, is the standing gospel norm.
  • UL 255.4. White: "a provision has been made whereby we may overcome.... He who truly believes in Christ is made partaker of the divine nature, and has power that he can appropriate under every temptation. He will not fall under temptation or be left to defeat." — the provision covers EVERY temptation; "he will not fall."
  • RH January 14, 1909, par. 6. White, a second witness: "In time of trial he will claim the promises, and by these escape the corruptions that are in the world through lust." — the way of escape of 1 Cor. 10:13 is taken by claiming the promises in the moment of trial.

Grace sufficient — strength perfected in the very weakness — 2 Cor. 12:9; Phil. 4:13:

  • 2 Cor. 12:9. "My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness." — provision matched precisely to weakness; His strength is perfected exactly where we are weakest, so no infirmity is an excuse for sin.
  • Phil. 4:13. "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me." — "all things": nothing God requires lies outside the enabling of the indwelling Christ.
  • MH 482.3. White: "Said the tried apostle Paul: 'He said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for My strength is made perfect in weakness.... for when I am weak, then am I strong.'" — the very infirmities that seem to excuse defeat are where the power of Christ rests.
  • SC 47.1. White: "Everything depends on the right action of the will.... You can give Him your will; He will then work in you to will and to do according to His good pleasure. Thus your whole nature will be brought under the control of the Spirit of Christ." — where the provision is appropriated: the believer yields the will, God works the doing; the choice to serve God is always available, so no known sin need be retained.

Even as I also overcame — the same victory, in the same flesh — Heb. 4:15; Rev. 3:21; 2:7; 3:12:

  • Heb. 4:15. "was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin" — Christ met temptation on our ground, in our infirmities, and did not fall: proof that being tempted never makes sinning inevitable (the flesh He met it in: see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took").
  • Rev. 3:21. "To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame" — the capstone: the SAME victory, held to the same standard, by the same faith, in the same flesh; Christ's overcoming is the pattern, not an exception.
  • Rev. 2:7. "To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life" — every church-letter reward is conditioned "to him that overcometh"; the overcomer is the assumed normal Christian, and Eden restored is his inheritance.
  • Rev. 3:12. "Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out" — the overcomer's final settled security; the reiterated promise fixes overcoming as the condition Christ everywhere expects and enables.
  • 3SM 139.3. White guards the "even as" from every escape-hatch: "If Christ had a special power which it is not the privilege of man to have, Satan would have made capital of this matter.... a man, tempted as a man, rendering the obedience of a man." — no advantage unavailable to us; the victory is genuinely reproducible.
  • ST January 8, 1902, par. 11. White: "He asked and received power to enable Him to overcome in the conflict. And those who walk in God's way may have the same power.... As He overcame, so we may overcome." — same power, same victory; and He commands "Be ye therefore perfect" because "He knows that it is possible" — the mark is not lowered.
  • 3SM 195.3. White answers the section's question in so many words: "Shall we keep on sinning as though it were an impossibility for us to overcome? How are we to overcome? As Christ overcame, and that is the only way.... I will cooperate with divine power and through grace be conqueror." — no, we need not keep on sinning; the will, refusing surrender to Satan, co-operates with divine power.
  • CH 574.1. White marks the cost: "It is only through obedience and continual effort that we shall overcome as Christ overcame." — the victory is real and reproducible, but not automatic; many desire the overcomer's reward who are not willing to endure the overcomer's toil, self-denial, and watching.

The mark never lowered — the Advocate for a fall that is possible, never necessary — 1 John 2:1; Matt. 1:21; Titus 2:14:

  • 1 John 2:1. "these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father" — the aim stated plainly: "that ye sin not"; the Advocate is the provision for the one who DOES fall, but the "if" guards the mark — falling is possible, never necessary, and the standard is never lowered to managed failure.
  • Matt. 1:21. "thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins" — His very name is the errand: salvation FROM sins, not accommodation in them; a gospel of managed failure contradicts the name Jesus (see "What Salvation Really Is — Saved From Sin").
  • Titus 2:14. "that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works" — ALL iniquity: the redemption's design is complete cleansing, not partial; no known sin need be retained.
  • COL 69.1. White: "Christ is waiting with longing desire for the manifestation of Himself in His church. When the character of Christ shall be perfectly reproduced in His people, then He will come to claim them as His own." — complete victory — Christ's own character in His people — is not an unreachable ideal but the very thing heaven waits for (ripened in "The Harvest — A People in Whom Christ Is Vindicated").

DEFINITION — COMPLETE VICTORY — OVERCOMING AS HE OVERCAME = the answer of Scripture to "must we always fall short?" is a charter of promises with no exception clause: sin "shall not have dominion" (Rom. 6:14) because the old man is crucified with Christ and the body of sin destroyed (Rom. 6:6), leaving the believer "made free from sin" (Rom. 6:22) — and Waggoner presses the plain sense: we ought never to sin any more, for Christ is able to keep the fully surrendered (WOR 198.5; WOR 110.3). The Son of God was manifested to DESTROY the works of the devil (1 John 3:8), and the born-of-God life does not practise sin while the seed remains (1 John 3:9; 5:18); the overcomer overcomes by "even our faith" (1 John 5:4) — the identical victory-faith by which Christ Himself overcame, given free to every man (CWCP 50.1). The provision is complete on every side: able to keep from falling (Jude 24), a way of escape with every temptation (1 Cor. 10:13), always caused to triumph (2 Cor. 2:14), grace sufficient and strength perfected in the very weakness we would plead as excuse (2 Cor. 12:9; Phil. 4:13; MH 482.3) — so no temptation compels sin, no infirmity excuses it, no known sin need be retained (Titus 2:14), and the believer "will not fall under temptation or be left to defeat" (UL 255.4; RH January 14, 1909). The means is faith, appropriated at the one point man controls — the will (SC 47.1; 3SM 195.3). The standard is Christ's own overcoming, "even as I also overcame" (Rev. 3:21), tempted in all points yet without sin, in the same flesh (Heb. 4:15; see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took"), by no special power unavailable to us (3SM 139.3; ST January 8, 1902), through obedience and continual effort (CH 574.1) — and it is the assumed condition of every church-letter promise (Rev. 2:7; 3:12). The mark is never lowered: "that ye sin not," with an Advocate if any man sin (1 John 2:1) — the fall possible, never necessary — for His name pledges salvation from sins (Matt. 1:21), His self-gift redeems from ALL iniquity (Titus 2:14), and He waits for His character to be perfectly reproduced in His people (COL 69.1).

Symbols defined here:

  • the overcomer = one in whom the born-of-God life triumphs over sin and the world — not by native strength but by Christ living out in fallen flesh the very victory He Himself won; the same faith (1 John 5:4), the same keeping (1 John 5:18), the same victory (Rev. 3:21, "even as I also overcame"; Gal. 2:20) — the normal Christian assumed by every church-letter promise (Rev. 2:7; 3:12), "made free from sin" (Rom. 6:22) under the charter "sin shall not have dominion" (Rom. 6:14).

Symbols carried: sin = the consented transgression of the law — the dominion here dethroned (see "What Sin Is — Transgression, Not Inheritance"); the flesh / fallen nature — the weakness in which grace is made perfect, enslaving only until Christ delivers (see "What Sin Is — Transgression, Not Inheritance"); the second Adam and sinful flesh — the nature in which the pattern-victory was won and in which we overcome (see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took"); the new birth — the "born of God" life of 1 John, by which the overcoming life is entered (see "Born of Water and of the Spirit — How He Lived, How We Begin"); salvation = saved FROM sin (see "What Salvation Really Is — Saved From Sin"); righteousness by faith — the faith that justifies is the same faith that overcomes, and this victory is its full fruit (see "Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel’s Message in Verity"); the faith of Jesus, defined in full at "The Commandments of God and the Faith of Jesus."

For discussion:

  1. Romans 6:14 is worded as a promise — "sin SHALL NOT have dominion over you" — not a command to try harder. Do we secretly read it as "sin should not"? What changes in the fight with a besetting sin when deliverance is trusted as God's pledged work through union with the crucified Christ (Rom. 6:6; 1 John 5:4) rather than attempted by our unaided resolve?
  2. 1 Corinthians 10:13 guarantees "with the temptation also a way to escape." Recall the last temptation you fell under: was there truly no escape — or an escape unused? In light of SC 47.1 — "you can give Him your will; He will then work in you" — what would "claiming the promises" (RH January 14, 1909) and giving God the will have looked like at that exact moment?
  3. Revelation 3:21 promises the throne "even as I also overcame," and 3SM 139.3 insists Christ had no special power unavailable to us. What excuse for a cherished sin does that leave — and what comfort does 1 John 2:1 add for the one who has fallen, without either truth lowering the mark "that ye sin not"?

Part IV — The Last Generation

¶8. The Commandments of God and the Faith of Jesus

The three angels' messages are the everlasting gospel in judgment-hour form, and they end by describing the people they produce — a patient company keeping BOTH the commandments of God AND the faith of Jesus: law and gospel held together, ripened to stand.

The everlasting gospel preached in the hour of judgment — Rev. 14:6-7; Rom. 1:16-17:

  • Rev. 14:6. "And I saw another angel fly in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting gospel to preach unto them that dwell on the earth, and to every nation, and kindred, and tongue, and people" — not a new gospel but the one eternal good news, borne worldwide in the last hour; whatever the three messages are, they are gospel first.
  • Rev. 14:7. "Fear God, and give glory to him; for the hour of his judgment is come: and worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters" — the gospel preached in a judgment-hour setting: fear God, give Him glory, worship the Creator — present truth because the hour of His judgment IS come.
  • 17LtMs, Lt 183, 1902, par. 4. White: "The subject of the first angel's message is the everlasting gospel" — the gospel is the substance the judgment-hour messages carry; take the gospel out and no message remains.
  • Rom. 1:16. "For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth" — the everlasting gospel of Rev. 14:6 is POWER, not mere information; it actually saves the believer it finds.
  • Rom. 1:17. "For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith." — the gospel reveals a righteousness of God received by faith; the message of Revelation 14 carries righteousness by faith (see "Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel's Message in Verity").

The judgment-hour call is the whole duty of man — Eccl. 12:13-14; Dan. 7:10:

  • Eccl. 12:13. "Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man" — the identical twofold call the first and third angels sound (Rev. 14:7, 12); the message is not a novelty but the conclusion of the whole matter.
  • Eccl. 12:14. "For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil" — Solomon's reason is the angel's reason: the duty is pressed because the judgment comes (Rev. 14:7).
  • Dan. 7:10. "thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened" — the heavenly courtroom whose hour has come (Rev. 14:7); the open books make the message urgent, for a people must be ripened who can stand there (see "The Time of Trouble — Standing Without a Mediator").

The third angel — two worships sorted, and a people described — Rev. 14:9, 12:

  • Rev. 14:9. "If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand" — the third angel's warning against false worship stands over against the true worship of v. 7; two loyalties are being sorted out in the judgment hour.
    • the third angel's message = the everlasting gospel (Rev. 14:6) in its judgment-hour form: righteousness by faith producing a commandment-keeping people — not law apart from gospel, for the message ends by describing the people it makes, who keep BOTH "the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus" (Rev. 14:9-12; Rom. 1:16-17; Eccl. 12:13-14; Dan. 7:10).
  • 1SM 372.2. White: "Several have written to me, inquiring if the message of justification by faith is the third angel's message, and I have answered, 'It is the third angel's message, in verity.'" — the keystone, her 1890 answer: Rev. 14:9-12 is gospel, the very righteousness by faith carried from "Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel's Message in Verity."
  • Rev. 14:12. "Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus." — the three messages END in a people: patient, commandment-keeping, holding the faith of Jesus — law and gospel together, neither alone.
    • the faith of Jesus = not merely faith IN Jesus (though it includes trust in His ability to save fully) but the faith OF Jesus — the very faith by which Christ Himself overcame, now living in the saints (Rev. 3:21, "even as I also overcame"; Heb. 12:2, "the author and finisher of our faith"; Gal. 2:20, "the faith of the Son of God"; 1 John 5:4) — the gospel half of the message that makes the law half possible.
  • CIHS 167.1. White: "The result of an acceptance of these messages is given in the word: 'Here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.' In order to be prepared for the judgment, it is necessary that men should keep the law of God. That law will be the standard of character in the judgment" — the messages are measured by their result: a people prepared to stand.
  • TMR 127.1. Smith: the message "is given in the period of the 'patience of the saints'... And this period of the saints' patience is marked by a most important fact, viz., the keeping of the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus" — the pioneer reading: the third message is identified by the people it produces.
  • AJB 301.1. Bates: "the third giving a most solemn warning against false worship, and presenting the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus" — the historical anchor: from the late 1840s the earliest Sabbatarian Adventists read the third message so; this is the doctrinal foundation of the movement.

The faith OF Jesus — the faith by which He overcame — Rev. 3:21; Heb. 12:2; Gal. 2:20:

  • Rev. 3:21. "To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne" — "even as I ALSO overcame": Christ overcame by faith in the flesh He took (see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took"), and grants the overcomer the same faith and the same seat (see "Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame").
  • Heb. 12:2. "Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross" — Jesus is not merely the object of faith but its author and finisher; He exercised faith Himself, enduring the cross, and that same faith He originates and perfects in the saints.
  • Gal. 2:20. "the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me" — the faith OF the Son of God living in the believer: Christ's own faith reproduced in the saint, the very mechanism by which the crucified-with-Christ life is lived out in the flesh.
  • CWCP 50.1. Jones: "That faith which He exercised and by which He obtained the victory over the world, the flesh, and the devil—that faith is His free gift to every lost man in the world" — the pioneer witness to the subjective-genitive sense: the faith by which Christ Himself overcame is the very faith He gives, which is the faith of Jesus the third angel's message names.
  • 3SM 172.3. White: "What constitutes the faith of Jesus, that belongs to the third angel's message? Jesus becoming our sin-bearer that He might become our sin-pardoning Saviour... He came to our world and took our sins that we might take His righteousness. And faith in the ability of Christ to save us amply and fully and entirely is the faith of Jesus." — EGW defines the symbol this section owns: trust in Christ's FULL ability to save, grounded in the great exchange.
  • TMR 134.2. Smith: "This term is used in distinction from the commandments of God... it is spoken of as being kept in the same manner that the commandments of God are kept" — Smith's own point reaches only this far: the faith of Jesus is the gospel half, distinct from yet kept alongside the law half. The overcoming-faith sense led with above is not Smith's reading but Jones's, on the Bible spine (Rev. 3:21; Heb. 12:2; Gal. 2:20; CWCP 50.1) — a Scripture-grounded sense wide enough to hold all three witnesses: the faith Jones names, which Christ exercised and gives freely; the faith EGW names, which trusts Christ's ability to save fully; and the gospel Smith names, kept as the commandments are kept.

That faith works by love and produces the keeping — 1 John 5:3-4; John 14:15:

  • 1 John 5:3. "For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous" — commandment-keeping is the fruit of love, not a burden set against the gospel; this is HOW they of Rev. 14:12 keep.
  • 1 John 5:4. "whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith" — the victory IS faith: the overcoming faith of Rev. 3:21 is the faith of Rev. 14:12, producing obedience in the born-again (see "Born of Water and of the Spirit — How He Lived, How We Begin").
  • John 14:15. "If ye love me, keep my commandments." — Christ's own order: love first, obedience following; the faith of Jesus working by love yields the commandment-keeping of Rev. 14:12.

The same twofold mark — the remnant the dragon wars against — Rev. 12:17; 19:10:

  • Rev. 12:17. "And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ." — the same twofold mark identifies the remnant; the people of Rev. 14:12 are the object of the dragon's final war.
  • Rev. 19:10. "the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy" — Scripture defines its own term: the second mark of the remnant is self-interpreted within the book.
  • TMR 114.1. Smith: "The preaching of the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus. This is the cause of the conflict between the dragon and the last fragment of the church... It is because the saints are keeping all the commandments of God that the dragon makes war upon them" — Rev. 14:12 and Rev. 12:17 name one people; the keeping provokes the war.

The book closes as chapter 14 described — Rev. 22:14:

  • Rev. 22:14. "Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city." — Revelation's last benediction falls on the very people the three messages produce; the commandment-keeping, faith-of-Jesus company inherits the city (see "The Harvest — A People in Whom Christ Is Vindicated").

DEFINITION — THE COMMANDMENTS OF GOD AND THE FAITH OF JESUS = the third angel's message is the everlasting gospel (Rev. 14:6; 17LtMs, Lt 183, 1902) preached in the hour of God's judgment (Rev. 14:7; Dan. 7:10; Eccl. 12:13-14) — the power of God unto salvation, revealing the righteousness of God by faith (Rom. 1:16-17) — righteousness by faith, "the third angel's message, in verity" (1SM 372.2; see "Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel's Message in Verity"). It is not law apart from gospel, for the messages END by describing the people they produce: "here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus" (Rev. 14:12; CIHS 167.1; TMR 127.1) — the same twofold-marked remnant the dragon wars against (Rev. 12:17; TMR 114.1), whose second mark Scripture self-interprets as the spirit of prophecy (Rev. 19:10). The faith of Jesus is the faith BY which He Himself overcame (Rev. 3:21; CWCP 50.1), which He authors and finishes (Heb. 12:2), which lives in the believer as His own life of faith reproduced (Gal. 2:20), and which trusts His ability "to save us amply and fully and entirely" (3SM 172.3) — the gospel half kept alongside the law half (TMR 134.2). That faith is itself "the victory that overcometh the world" (1 John 5:4), working by love to keep commandments that are not grievous (1 John 5:3; John 14:15). Law and gospel are therefore not rivals in the message but its two marks on one people: the commandments show what the faith of Jesus produces, and the faith of Jesus supplies what the commandments demand. The judgment-hour setting makes this present truth — the message must ripen a people who can stand when the books are opened (CIHS 167.1; see "The Time of Trouble — Standing Without a Mediator"), and the book closes as chapter 14 described: "they that do his commandments" enter through the gates into the city (Rev. 22:14; see "The Harvest — A People in Whom Christ Is Vindicated").

Symbols defined here:

  • the third angel's message = the everlasting gospel in its judgment-hour form: righteousness by faith producing a commandment-keeping people — never law apart from gospel (Rev. 14:6-7; Rev. 14:9-12; Rom. 1:16-17; 1SM 372.2; AJB 301.1).
  • the faith of Jesus = the very faith by which Christ overcame, authored and finished by Him, now living in the saints and producing commandment-keeping; trust in His ability to save amply, fully, and entirely (Rev. 14:12; Rev. 3:21; Heb. 12:2; Gal. 2:20; 1 John 5:3-4; CWCP 50.1; 3SM 172.3; TMR 134.2).

Symbols carried: righteousness by faith — imputed and imparted, here named as the message itself (see "Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel's Message in Verity"); the overcomer — the same victory, by the same faith, "even as I also overcame" (see "Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame"); the second Adam / sinful flesh — the flesh in which that overcoming faith was first lived (see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took"); sin as the consented transgression of the law the saints here keep (see "What Sin Is — Transgression, Not Inheritance").

For discussion:

  1. Rev. 14:12 names both "the commandments of God" and "the faith of Jesus." Which half do you naturally emphasize — and what would it look like this week to hold them as one message, where faith supplies what the law demands (1 John 5:3-4)?
  2. If the faith of Jesus is the very faith by which He overcame (Rev. 3:21; Gal. 2:20), what changes when temptation comes — trying harder, or trusting fuller in "the ability of Christ to save us amply and fully and entirely" (3SM 172.3)?
  3. "The hour of his judgment is come" (Rev. 14:7; Dan. 7:10) — the courtroom is already in session. How does that change what "present truth" means for your obedience and your witness today?

¶9. The Time of Trouble — Standing Without a Mediator

Before Christ comes, His intercession ceases and every character is fixed forever: the saints then live in the sight of a holy God without a mediator — plunged into the time of Jacob's trouble, yet saved out of it, because their sins went beforehand to judgment while the Advocate still pleaded.

Every case decided first — the cleansing of the sanctuary — Dan. 8:14; Rev. 3:5; Dan. 12:10:

  • Dan. 8:14. "Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed" — the cleansing of the sanctuary is the final phase of Christ's priestly work: the investigative judgment that decides every case before He ceases to intercede.
  • Rev. 3:5. "He that overcometh... I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels" — Christ's confession of the overcomer's name before the Father is His intercessory act, finished for each case in the judgment; the overcomer of "Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame" is the one whose name stands unblotted when the pleading ends.
  • Dan. 12:10. "Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly... but the wise shall understand" — the purifying is finished BEFORE Michael stands up; the victory work belongs to the hour when the Advocate still pleads.
  • GC 490.2. White: "When the work of the investigative judgment closes, the destiny of all will have been decided for life or death. Probation is ended a short time before the appearing of the Lord in the clouds of heaven" — the sanctuary-cleansing of Dan. 8:14 runs straight into the Rev. 22:11-12 decree.

The decree that closes probation — Rev. 22:11-12:

  • Rev. 22:11. "He that is unjust, let him be unjust still: and he which is filthy, let him be filthy still: and he that is righteous, let him be righteous still: and he that is holy, let him be holy still" — the word that fixes every character forever; no one changes sides after it is spoken.
    • the close of probation = the moment Christ's priestly mediation ends and every case is decided — each character sealed in what it has become, the decree spoken, the temple shut (Rev. 22:11-12; Rev. 15:8, "no man was able to enter into the temple"; Lev. 16:17; Dan. 8:14; Dan. 12:1). Defined in full at the close.
  • Rev. 22:12. "And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be" — the fixing of character and the rewarding advent are one connected event; the door of mercy shuts because He comes.
  • GC 613.2. White: "Then Jesus ceases His intercession in the sanctuary above. He lifts His hands and with a loud voice says, 'It is done;'... 'He that is unjust, let him be unjust still... and he that is holy, let him be holy still.' Revelation 22:11. Every case has been decided for life or death. Christ has made the atonement for His people and blotted out their sins" — the Rev. 22:11 decree IS the ceasing of intercession.
  • EW 71.2. White: "But there will be no time then to do it and no Mediator to plead their cause before the Father. Before this time the awfully solemn declaration has gone forth, 'He that is unjust, let him be unjust still... and he that is holy, let him be holy still'" — no Mediator after the declaration; whatever overcoming remains must be done before it.

The temple shut — no ministration while the plagues fall — Lev. 16:17; Rev. 15:8; 16:1:

  • Lev. 16:17. "And there shall be no man in the tabernacle of the congregation when he goeth in to make an atonement in the holy place, until he come out" — the type: while the high priest finishes the atonement, no man may be in the sanctuary; when he comes out, the atonement is done.
  • Rev. 15:8. "And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God, and from his power; and no man was able to enter into the temple, till the seven plagues of the seven angels were fulfilled" — the antitype: the heavenly sanctuary closed by God's own glory; no priest, no ministration, no intercession while the plagues fall.
  • Rev. 16:1. "Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth" — the plagues begin the instant the temple closes (15:8 → 16:1); the wrath is unmingled with mercy precisely because the Mediator no longer stands between God and man.
  • DAR 643.1. Smith: "there will therefore be no ministration in the sanctuary during this time... for Christ is then no longer a mediator; mercy, which has long stayed the hand of vengeance, pleads no more; the servants of God are all sealed" — the pioneer reading of Rev. 15:8: closed temple = ended mediation = a sealed people.
  • GC 614.1. White: "When He leaves the sanctuary, darkness covers the inhabitants of the earth. In that fearful time the righteous must live in the sight of a holy God without an intercessor" — the section's key phrase, matching the shut temple of Rev. 15:8.

Michael stands up — the trouble such as never was — Dan. 12:1:

  • Dan. 12:1. "And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation... and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book" — Christ rises from His mediatorial seat, His priestly work finished; the instant He ceases to intercede the unequalled trouble breaks — yet every name written in the book is delivered out of it.
  • MWV2 108.2. Miller: "Michael, in this passage, must mean Christ; he is the great Prince, and Prince of princes" — the earliest pioneer voice: Michael who "stands up" is Christ, the priestly Prince whose standing marks the end of His pleading.
  • GC 425.1. White: "Those who are living upon the earth when the intercession of Christ shall cease in the sanctuary above are to stand in the sight of a holy God without a mediator. Their robes must be spotless, their characters must be purified from sin by the blood of sprinkling" — the thesis in her own words: the purifying must be finished beforehand, because no mediator remains after.

The time of Jacob's trouble — the name and the type — Jer. 30:6-7; Gen. 32:24-28; Hos. 12:4:

  • Jer. 30:6. "wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into paleness?" — the anguish after mercy's door has shut: travail-pangs and pale faces, with no intercessor to plead the case.
  • Jer. 30:7. "Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble; but he shall be saved out of it" — the name text, matching Daniel's "such as never was"; the saints are not saved FROM the trouble but delivered THROUGH it.
    • the time of Jacob's trouble = the unequalled final anguish of the sealed saints after probation closes — the saints marked so the destroyer cannot touch them, wrestling without an intercessor as Jacob wrestled alone in the night, yet "saved out of it" (Jer. 30:6-7; Dan. 12:1; Gen. 32:24, 26, 28; Hos. 12:4; Rev. 7:3; Eze. 9:6). Defined in full at the close.
  • Gen. 32:24. "And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day" — the historical type: alone in the night, expecting Esau's sword, wrestling the Angel — the sealed saint pleading alone in the final crisis.
  • Gen. 32:26. "I will not let thee go, except thou bless me" — the language of the saints in the time of trouble: clinging in agony to a God whose face seems hidden, prevailing not by merit but by holding fast His covenant.
  • Gen. 32:28. "Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed" — the supplanter becomes the prince who prevails; the victory granted only because his sin had been confessed and put away before that night (GC 620.1).
  • Hos. 12:4. "Yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him" — the inspired commentary on the wrestling: he prevailed by tears and clinging prayer, not force; so the saints overcome by the wrestling of a heart that will not let God go.
  • GC 619.3. White: "They lay hold of the strength of God as Jacob laid hold of the Angel; and the language of their souls is: 'I will not let Thee go, except Thou bless me'" — Gen. 32:26 drawn straight onto the saints in the trouble.
  • GC 620.1. White: "if the people of God had unconfessed sins to appear before them while tortured with fear and anguish, they would be overwhelmed... But while they have a deep sense of their unworthiness, they have no concealed wrongs to reveal. Their sins have gone beforehand to judgment and have been blotted out" — why they can endure without a mediator: nothing remains on the books to condemn them.

Only the sealed stand — Rev. 7:3; Eze. 9:6; Mal. 3:2:

  • Rev. 7:3. "Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads" — before probation closes, the servants of God are sealed — settled into the truth so they cannot be moved; the sealing must be finished before the temple shuts (Rev. 15:8), and the sealed alone stand without a mediator.
  • Eze. 9:6. "but come not near any man upon whom is the mark: and begin at my sanctuary" — the type of the sealing before the slaughter: the destroyer may not touch any who bear the mark; and judgment begins at the house of God (cf. 1 Pet. 4:17).
  • Mal. 3:2. "But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner's fire, and like fullers' soap" — the question the whole crisis answers: only those refined BEFORE the day, cleansed by the blood while the Advocate still pleaded, can stand in the sight of a holy God without an intercessor.
  • COL 69.1. White: "When the character of Christ shall be perfectly reproduced in His people, then He will come to claim them as His own" — the character-perfecting must be finished while He pleads; the ripening of that people is the burden of "The Harvest — A People in Whom Christ Is Vindicated."

DEFINITION — THE TIME OF TROUBLE — STANDING WITHOUT A MEDIATOR = before the second coming Christ's priestly intercession ends: the cleansing of the sanctuary (Dan. 8:14) — the investigative judgment — decides every case while Christ still confesses names before the Father (Rev. 3:5), and the decree "he that is unjust, let him be unjust still... he that is holy, let him be holy still" fixes every character forever, "a short time before the appearing of the Lord" (Rev. 22:11-12; GC 490.2; GC 613.2; EW 71.2). The heavenly temple, like the tabernacle on the Day of Atonement (Lev. 16:17), is then shut — "filled with smoke... and no man was able to enter" (Rev. 15:8) — and the plagues fall unmingled with mercy (Rev. 16:1; DAR 643.1) while Michael, Christ the great Prince (MWV2 108.2), stands up from His mediatorial seat (Dan. 12:1). The saints then "live in the sight of a holy God without an intercessor" (GC 614.1; GC 425.1) — not without Christ's presence or the Spirit, but with every case decided — through "a time of trouble, such as never was," "even the time of Jacob's trouble" (Dan. 12:1; Jer. 30:7): like Jacob alone in the night they wrestle with travail-pangs and pale faces (Jer. 30:6; Gen. 32:24), clinging with "I will not let thee go, except thou bless me" (Gen. 32:26; GC 619.3), prevailing as he did by weeping and supplication (Hos. 12:4; Gen. 32:28). They endure only because the preparation was finished FIRST: purified, made white, and tried before Michael stood up (Dan. 12:10); sealed in their foreheads before the winds hurt (Rev. 7:3; Eze. 9:6); refined before the day that asks "who shall stand?" (Mal. 3:2); their "sins have gone beforehand to judgment and have been blotted out" (GC 620.1). This is why the victory message precedes the crisis — a people must cease from sin while the Advocate still pleads, that the character of Christ be perfectly reproduced before He comes to claim them (COL 69.1) — and it ends in deliverance: "he shall be saved out of it" (Jer. 30:7), "delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book" (Dan. 12:1).

Symbols defined here:

  • the close of probation = the moment Christ's priestly mediation ends and every character is fixed forever — every case decided in the cleansing of the sanctuary, the decree of Rev. 22:11 spoken because "I come quickly," the temple shut by the glory of God with no ministration while the plagues fall, Michael standing up from His mediatorial seat (Rev. 22:11-12; Rev. 15:8; Lev. 16:17; Dan. 8:14; Dan. 12:1).
  • the time of Jacob's trouble = the unequalled final anguish of the righteous after probation closes — the sealed saints, marked so the destroyer cannot touch them, wrestling without an intercessor as Jacob wrestled alone, prevailing by weeping and supplication because their sins have gone beforehand to judgment, and "saved out of it," every name written in the book (Jer. 30:6-7; Dan. 12:1; Gen. 32:24, 26, 28; Hos. 12:4; Rev. 7:3; Eze. 9:6).

Symbols carried: the overcomer — the one whose name Christ confesses and never blots out (see "Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame"); sin as consented transgression of the law — the saints stand here because they ceased from it while the Advocate still pleaded (see "What Sin Is — Transgression, Not Inheritance"); sinful flesh — the saints stand in the same fallen nature in which Christ overcame, He never having consented to sin (see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took"); the faith of Jesus and the third angel's message — the judgment-hour message that ripens the people who can stand (see "The Commandments of God and the Faith of Jesus"; see "Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel’s Message in Verity"); the character of Christ perfectly reproduced — ripened in full in "The Harvest — A People in Whom Christ Is Vindicated."

For discussion:

  1. The decree of Rev. 22:11 does not change anyone; it fixes each person in what he has already become. Jacob prevailed in his night of wrestling only because his sin had been confessed and put away before it came (Gen. 32:26-28; GC 620.1). What would the time of trouble find "unconfessed" in you if the decree went forth tonight — and what does it mean that the blotting out of sins is offered only NOW, while the Advocate still pleads (Rev. 3:5; Dan. 8:14)?
  2. Jacob prevailed not by force but by weeping and supplication (Hos. 12:4), and only because his sin was already confessed before that night (Gen. 32:28; GC 620.1, "their sins have gone beforehand to judgment"). How does daily confession now determine whether the hidden face of God then produces despair or prevailing prayer?
  3. Dan. 12:10 puts the purifying BEFORE the standing up of Michael: "many shall be purified, and made white, and tried." If the sealing settles the servants of God so they cannot be moved (Rev. 7:3; Eze. 9:6), which daily choices are settling you — into the truth, or into the "still" of Rev. 22:11 on the wrong side of it?

¶10. The Harvest — A People in Whom Christ Is Vindicated

The whole chain ends where the parable said it would: when the character of Christ is perfectly reproduced in His people the grain is ripe, the sickle falls, and in a faultless remnant the accuser is answered and God is vindicated before the watching universe.

The harvest law — the ripeness of the grain sets the hour of the sickle — Mark 4:26-29; Rev. 14:15; James 5:7-8:

  • Mark 4:26-27. "So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground; And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how" — the kingdom works as a crop works: sown, growing unseen, a fixed law moving toward a harvest.
  • Mark 4:28. "For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear" — growth is ordered and gradual, and its goal is not blade or ear but FULL corn: maturity.
  • Mark 4:29. "But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come" — the ripeness of the fruit, not a date on a calendar, brings the sickle; the moment the crop is ready, the reaping is IMMEDIATE.
    • the harvest / the ripe grain = the ripened likeness of Christ reproduced in His people — character matured from blade to full corn — which is itself the signal for the sickle; when the fruit is fully brought forth, Christ immediately reaps, so the ripeness of the crop sets the hour of His coming (Mark 4:28-29; Rev. 14:15, "the harvest of the earth is ripe"; James 5:7-8, the husbandman waiting for "the precious fruit of the earth"; Rev. 19:7-8, the wife made ready).
  • Rev. 14:15. "Thrust in thy sickle, and reap: for the time is come for thee to reap; for the harvest of the earth is ripe" — heaven's own reading of Mark 4:29 enacted at the end of the world: the time to reap IS the ripeness of the harvest; Christ comes when the crop is ready.
  • James 5:7. "...Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain" — the Husbandman Himself waits with long patience — not for time to pass but for grain to ripen under the two rains.
  • James 5:8. "Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh" — the coming draws nigh exactly as the fruit ripens; the waiting saints and the waiting Lord wait for the same thing.
  • COL 69.1. White: "Christ is waiting with longing desire for the manifestation of Himself in His church. When the character of Christ shall be perfectly reproduced in His people, then He will come to claim them as His own." — the keystone, written directly on Mark 4:29: the ripe fruit IS the reproduced character of Christ; He tarries for the harvest of His own likeness, then comes.
  • DA 671.2. White: "Christ has given His Spirit as a divine power to overcome all hereditary and cultivated tendencies to evil, and to impress His own character upon His church." — how the grain ripens: the Spirit overcomes every hereditary and cultivated tendency to evil and stamps Christ's character on the church — the birth of "Born of Water and of the Spirit — How He Lived, How We Begin" grown to full corn.

The sealed firstfruits — the 144,000 stand with the Lamb — Rev. 7:2-4; 14:1-5; Zeph. 3:13:

  • Rev. 7:2-3. "Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads" — the winds of strife are held back until the servants of God are sealed; the sealing must finish before the end can break.
  • Rev. 7:4. "And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel" — the sealed company numbered and named.
    • the 144,000 / the remnant = the last generation — the sealed servants of God, redeemed from among men as firstfruits, who follow the Lamb whithersoever He goeth and in whose mouth is found no guile: without fault before the throne, the remnant of Israel that shall not do iniquity nor speak lies; in them the gospel's full power is demonstrated (Rev. 7:2-4; Rev. 14:1-5; Zeph. 3:13; Eph. 5:27; Jude 1:24).
  • LDE 219.4. White: "Just as soon as the people of God are sealed in their foreheads—it is not any seal or mark that can be seen, but a settling into the truth, both intellectually and spiritually, so they cannot be moved—just as soon as God's people are sealed and prepared for the shaking, it will come." — the seal defined: a settling into truth so fixed the sealed cannot be moved — the inward reality behind the faultless standing.
  • Rev. 14:1. "a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father's name written in their foreheads" — the sealed of Rev. 7 seen standing with the Lamb; the seal is the FATHER'S NAME — His character — written in the mind.
  • Rev. 14:3. "they sung as it were a new song before the throne... and no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth" — a song of experience no other company can learn; their history is unrepeatable.
  • Rev. 14:4. "...These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men, being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb" — FIRSTFRUITS: harvest language again — the first ripe sheaf of the field, proof that the harvest law has run its full course in human flesh.
  • Rev. 14:5. "And in their mouth was found no guile: for they are without fault before the throne of God" — the crowning trait of the last generation: guileless mouths, faultless standing — and not before men, but before the THRONE.
  • Zeph. 3:13. "The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid" — the Old Testament twin of Rev. 14:5: the remnant shall NOT DO iniquity, and no deceit is in their mouth — salvation from sin demonstrated in a people (see "What Salvation Really Is — Saved From Sin").
  • SSP 250.1. Haskell: "In their mouth was found no guile; for the soul temple had been so thoroughly cleansed before leaving earth that the human mouth became a channel for the words of God.... This will be the mind of those who are sealed. They are without fault; because Christ's righteousness covers them as a garment.... They overcame by the blood of the Lamb." — three of the section's own terms in one witness — no guile, without fault, overcame by the blood — with Zeph. 3:13 in its printed margin; the faultlessness is Christ's righteousness as a garment, not human merit.

Faultless — kept and presented by His power, not their merit — Jude 1:24; Eph. 5:27; Rev. 19:7-8:

  • Jude 1:24. "Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy" — the keeping and the presenting are both HIS act: "faultless" (Rev. 14:5) is a doxology to His ability, not a boast of theirs.
  • Eph. 5:27. "That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish" — HE presents it to HIMSELF: the spotless church is Christ's own workmanship, the end for which He gave Himself.
  • Rev. 19:7. "the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready" — the readiness is real: the ripeness is actual, not a legal fiction; the harvest and the wedding are one event under two figures.
  • Rev. 19:8. "And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints" — "made herself ready," yet the arraying "was GRANTED": the righteousness of saints is a granted robe — righteousness by faith to the very end (see "Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel’s Message in Verity").
  • 1SM 366.1. White: "God requires the entire surrender of the heart, before justification can take place; and in order for man to retain justification, there must be continual obedience, through active, living faith that works by love and purifies the soul." — the granted robe and the actual obedience are not rivals: the harvest of a guileless people is justification by faith retained and ripened, not a work replacing it.

The vindication — the accuser answered before the watching universe — Eph. 3:10; Rev. 12:10-11:

  • Eph. 3:10. "To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God" — the demonstration has an audience: the unfallen universe learns the wisdom of God BY THE CHURCH.
  • 16MR 115.1. White: "In heaven Satan had declared that the sin of Adam revealed that human beings could not keep the law of God.... Christ came to unmask the deceiver.... The Majesty of heaven would undertake the cause of man, and with the same facilities that man may obtain, stand the test and proving of God as man must stand it." — the charge on trial: that the law cannot be kept in human flesh; Christ answered it "with the same facilities that man may obtain" (see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took").
  • Rev. 12:10. "Now is come salvation... for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night" — courtroom language: Satan is the ACCUSER, and the day-and-night accusation is silenced not by argument but by evidence.
  • Rev. 12:11. "And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death" — the evidence named: THEY overcame HIM, by the blood and by testimony; the vindication of God is worked out in overcomers.
  • DA 671.3. White: "The very image of God is to be reproduced in humanity. The honor of God, the honor of Christ, is involved in the perfection of the character of His people." — the stake named plainly: God's own honor rides on the perfected character of His people — the manifold wisdom of Eph. 3:10 shown in the last generation.

"Even as I also overcame" — the whole chain ripens here — Rev. 3:21:

  • Rev. 3:21. "To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne" — the last promise to the last church: the overcomer's victory is of one kind with Christ's own — same nature, same power, same throne.
  • 2SP 39.3. White: "It was in the order of God that Christ should take upon himself the form and nature of fallen man, that he might be made perfect through suffering, and himself endure the strength of Satan's fierce temptations..." — the ground of "even as I": He overcame in the nature of fallen man, the very flesh in which the accuser said the law could not be kept (see "The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took").
  • CWCP 84.1. Jones: "Perfection, perfection of character, is the Christian goal—perfection attained in human flesh in this world. Christ attained it in human flesh in this world and thus made and consecrated a way by which, in Him, every believer can attain it." — the pioneer spine: the harvest is attainable because the Forerunner already ripened in this soil (see "Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame").
  • GC 425.1. White: "Those who are living upon the earth when the intercession of Christ shall cease in the sanctuary above are to stand in the sight of a holy God without a mediator. Their robes must be spotless, their characters must be purified from sin by the blood of sprinkling.... This work is more clearly presented in the messages of Revelation 14." — the ripe grain and the close of intercession joined — and joined by the witness herself to Revelation 14 (see "The Time of Trouble — Standing Without a Mediator").
  • GC 614.1. White: "When He leaves the sanctuary, darkness covers the inhabitants of the earth. In that fearful time the righteous must live in the sight of a holy God without an intercessor." — the setting of the final demonstration: the sealed stand faultless while no mediator pleads — the harvest standing ripe in the field after the rain has ceased.
  • COL 415.5. White: "The last rays of merciful light, the last message of mercy to be given to the world, is a revelation of His character of love. The children of God are to manifest His glory. In their own life and character they are to reveal what the grace of God has done for them." — the message and the demonstration are one thing: the third angel's message ends as a people in whom the character it preached is visible (see "The Commandments of God and the Faith of Jesus").

DEFINITION — THE HARVEST — A PEOPLE IN WHOM CHRIST IS VINDICATED = the end of the whole chain is a crop. The kingdom grows as grain grows — first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn — and "when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come" (Mark 4:26-29): the ripeness of the grain, not an arbitrary date, sets the hour of the sickle (Rev. 14:15), and the Husbandman waits with long patience through early and latter rain for "the precious fruit of the earth" (James 5:7-8). The ripe fruit is the character of Christ perfectly reproduced in His people (COL 69.1), wrought by the Spirit overcoming every hereditary and cultivated tendency to evil (DA 671.2). The reaped sheaf is the 144,000 — sealed in their foreheads before the winds break (Rev. 7:2-4), settled into the truth so they cannot be moved (LDE 219.4), bearing the Father's name, following the Lamb whithersoever He goeth, firstfruits unto God, "and in their mouth was found no guile: for they are without fault before the throne of God" (Rev. 14:1-5) — the remnant that "shall not do iniquity" (Zeph. 3:13). Their faultlessness is His act, not their merit: He is "able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless" (Jude 1:24); He presents to Himself a church without spot or wrinkle (Eph. 5:27); the bride's readiness is a GRANTED arraying in the righteousness of saints (Rev. 19:7-8), Christ's righteousness covering them as a garment (SSP 250.1), justification by faith retained through living obedience (1SM 366.1). And the demonstration has an audience: by the church the manifold wisdom of God is made known to principalities and powers (Eph. 3:10); Satan's ancient charge — that the law cannot be kept in human flesh (16MR 115.1) — is answered when a people overcome the accuser "by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony" (Rev. 12:10-11), overcoming "even as I also overcame" (Rev. 3:21): in the same fallen nature Christ took (2SP 39.3), by the way He consecrated in human flesh (CWCP 84.1), standing at last without a mediator in spotless robes (GC 425.1; GC 614.1). Here every thread of the handbook ripens — the living soul in whom the ripening happens ("Dust and Breath — What Man Is"), sin as transgression ("What Sin Is — Transgression, Not Inheritance"), the nature Christ took ("The Second Adam — The Nature Christ Took"), the new birth ("Born of Water and of the Spirit — How He Lived, How We Begin"), salvation from sin ("What Salvation Really Is — Saved From Sin"), the granted robe ("Righteousness by Faith — The Third Angel’s Message in Verity"), the overcomer ("Complete Victory — Overcoming as He Overcame"), the judgment-hour message ("The Commandments of God and the Faith of Jesus"), the standing without an intercessor ("The Time of Trouble — Standing Without a Mediator") — for the honor of God is involved in the perfection of the character of His people (DA 671.3), and the last message of mercy is His character of love made visible in them (COL 415.5). When that fruit is brought forth, immediately He puts in the sickle.

Symbols defined here:

  • the harvest / the ripe grain = the ripened likeness of Christ reproduced in His people — character matured from blade to full corn — which is itself the signal for the sickle; the ripeness of the crop, not an arbitrary date, sets the hour of His coming (Mark 4:26-29; Rev. 14:15; James 5:7-8; Rev. 19:7-8; COL 69.1).
  • the 144,000 / the remnant = the last generation — the sealed servants of God, redeemed from among men as firstfruits, following the Lamb whithersoever He goeth, without guile and without fault before the throne, the remnant of Israel that shall not do iniquity nor speak lies; in them the gospel's power is demonstrated and God is vindicated (Rev. 14:1-5; Rev. 7:2-4; Zeph. 3:13; Eph. 5:27; Jude 1:24; LDE 219.4).
